NONE: › someone who collects things that they do not need
（收藏的東西都是自己不需要的）垃圾收藏家

example: For me there could be nothing worse than living with a pack rat.
對我來說，最討厭的事情，莫過於和一個垃圾收藏家住在一起。

NONE: › an important part of the history of a place, time, or group of people
歷史上的一頁

example: The signing of the peace treaty will be seen as a glorious page in our country's history.
和平條約的簽訂將被視為我國歷史上光輝的一頁。

NONE: B2 someone or something that is very annoying
極其討厭的人（或事物）

example: That child is a real pain in the neck.
那個孩子真討厭。

NONE: › someone or something that is very annoying
極其討厭的人（或事物）

example: The kids were a real pain in the arse.
這些孩子真討厭。

NONE: › the activity of dealing with many different documents in order to achieve something
文檔追索搜集，大量文案工作

example: To receive even the smallest amount of financial aid from a college, it's a real paper chase.
想要獲得大學的最少量的財政補助，也都要先處理填妥數之不盡的文件。

NONE: › the point at which two people or organizations separate
分手（或拆夥）的時刻

example: The parting of the ways came after a series of disagreements between the singer and his song-writer.
經過一連串爭執後，歌手和他的曲作者最終各奔東西。

NONE: › a slightly similar appearance
些許的相似

example: He bears more than a passing resemblance to (= he is noticeably similar to) the young Marlon Brando.
他長得頗像年輕時的馬龍‧白蘭度。

NONE: › praise
稱讚，讚揚

example: I got a pat on the back from (= was praised by) my boss.
我得到了老闆的稱讚。

NONE: › something that is very rare and is considered very important
珍貴罕見之物

example: Inexhaustible patience is a pearl of great price.
無盡的耐心是難能可貴的。

NONE: › something you say that means it is wise to save money
能省則省；省一文賺一文

example: I'd advise anyone to put aside a proportion of their earnings - a penny saved is a penny earned.
我建議人們把收入的一部分存起來——儲蓄一文賺一文。

NONE: › involvement in something successful that someone else has started
參與或插手（他人成功之事）；分一杯羹

example: Now research has proved that the drug is effective, everyone wants a slice of the action.
目前研究證明這種藥的確有效，所以大家都想趁機分一杯羹。

NONE: › part of the profit or benefit from something, or part of the amount of something that is available
可以得到的一份（盈利或福利）

example: The company plans to acquire new businesses to grab a bigger piece of the pie.
公司計畫通過兼併來分享更大的利益。
People see others getting pay raises and they want a slice of the pie.
人們看到別人漲工資就想自己也該得一份。

NONE: › something that you buy or accept without first seeing it or finding out if it is good
盲目購買（或接受）的東西
› This means that the best way to stay well organized is to keep things in their correct positions.
物歸其所就會乾淨整潔。
› a good or lucky position
好位置；幸運的位置

example: He certainly earned his place in the sun.
他確實得到了一個令人艷羨的位置。

NONE: › a problem that politicians from different parties argue about and try to use in order to get an advantage for themselves
政治足球（各黨派政治家爭論並試圖利用以獲取好處的問題）

example: We don't want the immigration issue to become a political football.
我們不想讓移民問題成為政治足球。

NONE: › a bad situation
糟糕的局面

example: Things have come to a pretty pass when a referee can no longer be trusted.
當裁判不再可信時，情況就很糟糕了。

NONE: › a very difficult and annoying situation
難辦的事；尷尬的局面
› relating to an argument that suggests the probable effects of a known cause, or using general principles to suggest likely effects
由因及果的；由一般到具體的；演繹的

example: "It's freezing outside; you must be cold" is an example of a priori reasoning.
「外面結冰了，你一定會感到很冷」是一種由因及果的推理。

NONE: › used to say that if you tell someone about a problem, it is easier to deal with
有人分擔，憂愁減半。
› said when you want to know what another person is thinking, usually because they have been quiet for a while
你在想甚麼呢
